newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega-Bandai aims for 50 bln yen profit in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Sega-Bandai aims for 50 bln yen profit in 97/98.

text.p: Hayao Nakayama, president of Sega Enterprises Ltd, said on Thursday that he hopes the new company to be formed out of its merger with Bandai Co Ltd will post a group profit of 50 billion yen in the 1997/98 fiscal year.

Nakayama told a news conference that the merger plan, which was announced earlier on Thursday and is to take effect on October 1, was designed to take advantage of a larger scale of business and to enhance international competitiveness.
The companies said in a statement that the merged company would be a formidable new force in the toy and videogame market with annual group sales surpassing 600 billion yen.
"We would like to become a global, comprehensive, new entertainment company and expand further internationally," Nakayama said.
"In order to do so, the scale of 600 billion yen (in sales) is very significant," he added.
In the merger, one Bandai share will be exchanged for 0.76 Sega shares, the two companies said. Bandai will be dissolved as a result of the merger, they said.

"If the new company expands its global operations, even big names like Sony and Matsushita (Electric Industrial Co Ltd) will become our competitors," said Nakayama, who will become vice chairman of the new company.
The companies began discussing the merger, which was first raised by Sega, late last year, he said.
Bandai, a leading Japanese toy producer, is best known for its Power Ranger series of toys and has recently scored a hit with a "virtual pet" that it says is a sellout success.
Sega is a leading producer of video games for both the home and arcade market but has been facing problems recently due to stiff competition.
Bandai president Makoto Yamashina will become president of Sega-Bandai, and Sega chairman Isao Ohkawa will become its chairman.
